text: What does it mean to say a HoTT proof 'computes' π₄(S³)?
choices: It uses a computer algebra system
The proof term, when normalised, produces the canonical element ℤ/2ℤ — the actual mathematical answer
explanation: A computational proof means the proof term reduces (β/η-normalises) to the actual value. Brunerie's proof term for π₄(S³)=ℤ/2ℤ was computationally verified (Cubical Agda normalised it to ℤ/2ℤ).
